clue.text: But does he really put years on those he controls?

definitions.text: But does he really put years on those he controls?

parts.words: But does he really put years on those he controls?
parts.note: split the word for a boss into MAN and a word for one who makes people older: a boss is one who might age the men under him

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether bosses age their staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss who directs staff is the person running a team or business.

clue.text: Bluestocking's complaint?

parts.note: a learned woman might be an MA and a lady, so the illness is pictured as her title

explanation.surface: What ails an intellectual woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A bluestocking is a scholarly woman; read the answer as MA plus LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or ailment is a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Disconcert nobody, some say, taking more

indicators.note: some say means the word for nobody is heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: nobody means none
plus means more, in addition

explanation.surface: Upsetting nobody while grabbing extra.
explanation.definitionFit: To perplex someone so they don't know what to do is to throw them.

clue.text: Saw lagers being drunk out of tumblers

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and muddled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone saw beers being drunk from glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers are drinking glasses, items of glass tableware.

clue.text: Ophidian frightens Ken — a mistake

parts.note: rattles means unnerves, frightens

indicators.note: mistake signals the letters of Ken and a are wrongly placed

explanation.surface: A snake scares Ken, who made an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means relating to snakes; this venomous American serpent is one.

clue.text: Offer too much for surplus tender

parts.note: a surplus is what is left over, an excess
to tender is to offer, as a bid does at auction

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction paying more than a surplus item is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: At auction, bidding beyond the value is putting in a price higher than warranted.

clue.text: Poetically superior to the sweep, say

indicators.note: say means what follows is pronounced like another word

parts.note: a sweep is a long oar used to row a boat

explanation.surface: A poet claims to be above a chimney sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweep' suggests chimneys; here it is a long oar. 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic contraction of 'over' means above.

clue.text: Once the law of demand

parts.note: ex- means former, once
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: A former statute of demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to insist on or require payment, to demand it.

clue.text: Concealed microphone a semi-blunder-it causes annoyance

parts.note: a bug is a hidden listening device

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word for a blunder is used

parts.note: a booboo is a blunder

explanation.surface: A hidden mike being a half-blunder that irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear, a source of dread or irritation, is a thing that annoys.

clue.text: Administer a girl's money soundly

indicators.note: soundly means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Di's pence: the money of Di, a girl's name

explanation.surface: Managing a young woman's cash sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out medicine or justice is to deal it out.

clue.text: Cavalryman protecting a way to the Royal House

indicators.note: the cavalryman's word wraps round and so guards the other letters

parts.note: a lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier guarding a road to a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lancaster was one side in England's medieval Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty of Henry IV, V and VI was an English ruling family, a royal house.

clue.text: Article, for instance, is a form of sponsorship

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar remark that an article is a kind of backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's protection or patronage, as in 'under the auspices of', means backed by them.

clue.text: Guy's companions are young girls

definitions.meaning: in the musical Guys and ... the guys are paired with their sweethearts
old slang for pretty girls, and the toys little girls play with

explanation.surface: A man's female friends described as rather young.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical title pairs guys with their women, and the word is also dated slang for attractive young women.

clue.text: Can be found in the new Coal Board

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: Something is discoverable within the newly formed National Coal Board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coal Board' looks like one name, but 'Board' must first become TABLE; COAL plus TABLE then rearranges under 'new'. The National Coal Board ran Britain's nationalised coal mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be tracked down or discovered is able to be pinpointed.

clue.text: Put many sadly into the shade for the duration

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, many

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone amiss, so the word into is jumbled

parts.note: a nuance is a shade of meaning

explanation.surface: Cast many sorrowfully into darkness for a long period.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuance means persistence for a length of time.

clue.text: One races after two idiots causing terrorist acts

indicators.note: after places the clue's opening pieces behind the idiots in the answer

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and two of them are given
an ass is a fool, and two of them are given
I is the Roman numeral one
races in the sense of peoples, nations

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting after a pair of fools, which provokes violent attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Political murders of public figures are classic acts of terror.

clue.text: Rise above a tendency to keep battered cans

indicators.note: to keep means the word for a tendency holds the other letters within

parts.note: a trend is a tendency

indicators.note: battered suggests something knocked out of shape, so cans is jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting above a habit of hoarding dented tins.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond or surpass limits is to rise above them.

clue.text: Points on books Williams finds obscure

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
Eric is a first name to go with Williams

explanation.surface: Someone named Williams finds the book's points hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few initiates, hence abstruse.

clue.text: Sally is catty with me, wrongly but on purpose

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters are put in the wrong order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Sally is being spiteful to me, unfairly but deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a thing methodically and deliberately, by design, is doing it on purpose.

clue.text: Initially confused clergyman?

parts.note: a cleric famous for swapping the first sounds of words, muddling them initially

explanation.surface: A vicar who is muddled at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rev William Archibald Spooner of Oxford gave his name to swapped initial sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford don and priest is the clergyman famous for mixing up initial letters.

clue.text: Lion-like Pope?

explanation.surface: A pope who resembles a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or like a lion; Pope Leo IX read in words.

clue.text: Chemistry is abominable

definitions.meaning: schoolboy slang for chemistry, from its smells

explanation.surface: A student's verdict that chemistry is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: British public-school slang calls chemistry by this name for its bad smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school slang names chemistry for its smells; to be awful is to reek.

clue.text: Bridal togs tailored originally by French artist

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word tailored

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A bride's clothes, custom-made and designed by a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for married life is her bridal outfit.

clue.text: Novelist is detailed and serious

indicators.note: de-tailed means the last letter of the novelist's name is removed

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A writer is described as meticulous and grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'meticulous'; read it as de-tailed, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe and grave in manner.

clue.text: He must be prepared to look for new players

definitions.meaning: talent spotters search for new players for a club

explanation.surface: A sports talent spotter must always be ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boy Scout follows the motto 'Be prepared'; a talent spotter searches out recruits.

clue.text: Hurried say, back to the mountains

parts.note: hurried means ran

indicators.note: back means the letters for 'say' are read from right to left

parts.note: say is a signal for an example, e.g.

explanation.surface: Someone rushed back to the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of peaks is a mountain range.

clue.text: I landed, unfortunately, on this plant

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone lands badly on a weed.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered weed of lawns is a common plant.

clue.text: Carrier comes up with note

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A postman arrives with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the first note of the scale is doh.

clue.text: A bit of decor in the City

indicators.note: only a piece of the words decor in the is wanted, a run within them

explanation.surface: A small piece of interior decoration in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' suggests London's financial district; it is the ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek city on the isthmus, famed for its columns and St Paul's letters, is a city.

clue.text: Continuing too long without a goal

parts.note: a goal is an end, an aim
-less is the suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: Something goes on and on with no aim.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'without a goal' as 'goal-less', with the suffix following.
explanation.definitionFit: Something interminable seems to go on forever.
